name: Anonymous marketplace alerts
description: Mobile and email alerts when a new item is listed on one large marketplace. There is also an API, and webhooks, so a reseller can plug the feed into a buying tool. Plans are $3 to $20 a month. Founded 1 December 2025. UK. The listing does not name the company or give a product site. The 30 October note is a French reseller tool at much higher prices. This is the cheap version of that idea.

mentions.evidence: The sync is Stripe and the App Store. MRR $382, up 20.3%. 29 subscriptions. Last-30-day margin 50% claimed. Last 30 days $1,159, up 38%. Last 12 months $3,270. Listed for sale on 30 October 2026 at $70,000 (5.0x), 0 offers. Revenue synced 30 October 2026 ~12:42 Warsaw.
mentions.indieAngle: The same alert, priced for a hobbyist, is a much smaller Stripe number than the professional listing from 30 October.

whyItPrints: A polling job and a notification. The price is hobbyist money, not professional-reseller money.
whyThisMatters:
A phone alert and an email when one big marketplace lists something new. Plans are a few dollars to twenty. There is also an API and a webhook, so a reseller can feed a buying tool. Started in December 2025. UK. No name. No site. The 30 October note is a French tool that does the same job at a much higher price. This is the cheap one.

Stripe and the App Store are both in the sync. I am not relabeling it as only one of them. A few dozen subscriptions. The last thirty days of cash are higher than the monthly line. The asking price is a high multiple of that small line, and nobody has offered. The lesson in the brief is the price: hobbyist plans and professional plans are not the same business.

You pay a few dollars so a new listing does not sit there unseen.
